title: Corporate holiday party catering in Dubai: what to confirm early
body_markdown:
For corporate Christmas catering in Dubai, confirm the event date, venue access, guest count, service format and dietary requirements before approving the menu. Ask for a written scope covering food, staffing, equipment, setup and clearing. A festive menu is only part of the booking; responsibility for service and the room’s handover needs to be clear too.


**TL;DR**

- Christmas catering Dubai enquiries should specify the venue, guest count, service format and dietary requirements before menu approval.
- myCHEF provides corporate event catering in Dubai; request a written proposal matched to your event brief.
- Compare proposals by staffing, equipment, service responsibilities and exclusions, not menu descriptions alone.
- Confirm venue access and the final guest-count deadline before committing to the event plan.


## What should you confirm early for corporate holiday party catering?

**Confirm the operating plan before choosing the festive finishing touches.** Start with the date, location, expected attendance and whether guests will sit, circulate or eat between presentations. These decisions shape the menu and the work required on site.

For wider supplier-selection questions, the [corporate event catering guide](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-corporate-event-catering-companies-in-dubai) provides a related starting point. This checklist focuses on what your event brief and proposal need to settle before approval.

1. **Event brief:** State the occasion, date, address, guest count and internal decision-maker.
2. **Venue check:** Establish access, preparation space, equipment and building restrictions.
3. **Service plan:** Choose the format and agree who handles each stage.
4. **Written approval:** Confirm the menu, responsibilities, exclusions and change deadlines.


![Four planning stages from the event brief to written catering approval](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/cfe14f94-50e7-4ab3-8aec-46b41dd19e5a/body-bbb005c690e17414bb59e9f66331f024.jpg)

*Settle the event requirements before approving the final catering scope.*


## Why does the service format matter before the menu?

A company drinks reception, an office lunch and a seated celebration need different service plans. Choose according to how you want colleagues to spend their time, not simply which dishes sound festive.

The comparison below describes planning options, not confirmed myCHEF packages. Ask your proposed caterer which formats they can deliver for your venue and brief.

| Format | Best for | Main advantage | Trade-off to confirm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drop-off catering | An office gathering with an internal host | Separates food delivery from event service | Your team needs an agreed plan for setup, replenishment and clearing |
| Staffed buffet | A shared meal with flexible seating | Lets guests choose their dishes | Requires serving space and a plan for queues and replenishment |
| Canapé reception | A standing celebration centred on conversation | Keeps the gathering focused on mingling | Portion planning must reflect whether food replaces dinner |
| Plated dinner | A seated celebration with a structured programme | Gives the meal a defined sequence | Requires coordinated seating, service and dietary meal identification |

Do not treat these as interchangeable descriptions on a quotation. A menu delivered to reception is a different scope from a team setting tables, serving guests and clearing afterwards.

**Choose the service format around the event programme.** If speeches are central, explain when food service should pause. If colleagues will arrive at different times, ask how the proposed format accommodates that pattern.

## What should the venue confirm before you request a proposal?

Give the caterer practical venue information, not just the address. Ask your office manager, facilities team or venue contact to confirm what outside catering involves at that particular location.

A Dubai office tower brief should address the delivery route, loading arrangements, service lift access and the person who authorises entry. These are questions for the building, not assumptions to leave with the catering team.

Check the following:

- **Access:** Where deliveries arrive, who receives them and how equipment reaches the event space.
- **Preparation:** Whether the caterer can use a kitchen, pantry or designated preparation area.
- **Facilities:** Which power, water, refrigeration and washing facilities are available for the proposed service.
- **Layout:** Where food, drinks, used crockery and equipment will sit.
- **Restrictions:** Any venue conditions affecting cooking, setup, deliveries or clearing.
- **Handover:** When the room must be ready and when it must be returned.

For a terrace or outdoor celebration, ask for an indoor alternative and a decision process if conditions make the original setup unsuitable. Have the venue approve the proposed arrangement before it becomes part of the final brief.

## How do you choose a festive menu for a mixed team?

Start with the role of the food. Is this a complete lunch, a dinner, or refreshments during a company celebration? State that explicitly so proposals answer the same question.

Then describe the balance you want between recognisable Christmas dishes and broader menu choices. Do not assume every colleague wants the same festive meal or that a traditional centrepiece answers every dietary requirement.

An **illustrative menu brief**, rather than a confirmed package, could request:

- A festive main dish with clearly described accompaniments.
- A substantial plant-based main, not just additional side dishes.
- Salads or vegetables selected to suit the service format.
- Desserts with ingredients and dietary suitability confirmed.
- A separate drinks scope stating what the caterer and host each provide.

Ask how dishes travel, hold and reach guests within the proposed setup. A dish intended for immediate plated service needs a different plan from food served throughout a buffet.

Keep menu approval separate from decorative choices. Confirm what guests will eat and how it will be served before discussing themed presentation, table styling or other optional additions.

## How should you brief dietary requirements and allergens?

Collect dietary information before approving the menu. Distinguish allergies from preferences, religious requirements and ingredient exclusions; a general request for a varied menu does not communicate these needs.

Ask guests to describe their requirements clearly through an appropriate internal contact. Share the catering-relevant information with the supplier, without circulating unnecessary personal details.

Your approval process should establish:

- Which dishes suit each stated requirement.
- How ingredients and potential cross-contact will be discussed.
- How the team will identify special meals during service.
- Who answers ingredient questions at the event.
- What happens if a requirement changes after menu approval.

Do not describe a meal as allergy-safe on the supplier’s behalf. **Ask the caterer to confirm what they can accommodate and how they will handle it.** Where a requirement cannot be met, resolve the alternative before the event rather than at the serving table.

## What should the written catering proposal include?

A useful proposal makes responsibilities visible. You should be able to identify what arrives, who works on site and what remains your team’s responsibility without interpreting broad phrases such as full service.

Ask for a scope that separates the following elements:

| Scope item | What to confirm |
|---|---|
| Food | Approved dishes, service format and portion assumptions |
| Staffing | Roles, attendance window and responsibility for service |
| Equipment | Preparation, serving and holding equipment included or required |
| Tableware | Crockery, cutlery, glassware, napkins and collection arrangements |
| Drinks | Supply, serving, ice and glassware responsibilities |
| Setup | Delivery, room preparation and readiness time |
| Clearing | Food-service clearing, washing, waste handling and room handover |
| Changes | Guest-count deadline, menu amendments and approval process |

For myCHEF corporate catering, request a proposal built around your business event rather than assuming household chef arrangements apply. The booking needs to describe the celebration you are organising.

The guide to [serving staff and catering cleanup](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/can-catering-companies-in-dubai-provide-serving-staff-and-cleanup) addresses a useful follow-up question. Confirm the actual responsibilities in your own proposal; a general guide is not a booking term.

## Why do corporate holiday catering proposals vary?

Different proposals can describe different amounts of work. Before comparing totals, check that each supplier has received the same brief and included the same responsibilities.

These are the main scope differences to examine:

- **Guest count:** State the expected attendance and how the final number will be confirmed.
- **Menu:** Compare the actual dishes, dietary alternatives and portion assumptions.
- **Service format:** Separate delivered food from staffed buffet, reception or plated service.
- **Staffing:** Check roles and attendance windows rather than comparing an unexplained team total.
- **Equipment and access:** Identify what the venue supplies and what must be brought in.
- **Setup and clearing:** Establish the work included before guests arrive and after they leave.

**Compare like-for-like scopes before choosing a proposal.** If a line is unclear, ask the supplier to explain it in writing instead of filling the gap with an assumption.

## When should you settle the guest count and event schedule?

Ask the caterer for their specific confirmation deadlines during the enquiry. There is no reason to treat a suggested planning timeline as a universal booking rule.

Separate your working estimate from the final catering number. Explain whether attendance includes employees only, invited clients, partners or other guests, and identify who can authorise a change.

Build the schedule around milestones rather than an arbitrary countdown:

- **Before proposal approval:** Agree the venue, service format, estimated attendance and main dietary requirements.
- **Before the supplier’s deadline:** Confirm the final guest count and approved menu changes.
- **Before event day:** Circulate access instructions, supplier contacts and the agreed running order.
- **At handover:** Check the setup against the approved plan and identify the event-day decision-maker.

Include arrival, food service, speeches and clearing in the same running order. Give the venue and caterer the same version so neither team is working from an outdated schedule.

## Who should own decisions on the day?

Nominate an organiser and a backup. Give the catering lead a clear route for questions about access, service timing and authorised changes.

Your organiser does not need to supervise every plate. They do need to know what was agreed and who can resolve a problem with the room, equipment or event schedule.

**myCHEF corporate catering is for businesses planning catered events in Dubai.** Use the enquiry to explain the event’s purpose and practical requirements; confirm menu choices, staffing and service boundaries in the resulting proposal.

Before approval, ask your internal team a simple question: if nobody from the office helps with service, does the proposed scope still cover the event? For drop-off catering, the answer will depend on the responsibilities you have assigned internally.

## FAQ


**What should I confirm first for Christmas catering in Dubai?**

Confirm the date, venue, expected guest count and service format first. Then provide dietary requirements and ask for a written scope covering food, staffing, equipment, setup and clearing.

**Is drop-off catering enough for an office Christmas party?**

Drop-off catering suits an office party when your team has agreed responsibility for setup, replenishment and clearing. If you want those tasks handled externally, ask for an appropriately staffed proposal.

**Can we request traditional Christmas food and plant-based dishes?**

Request both in the initial menu brief and ask the caterer to confirm the dishes they can provide. A plant-based main should be planned as a complete meal rather than left as a selection of side dishes.

**Does corporate catering include plates, serving staff and cleanup?**

Plates, serving staff and cleanup need explicit confirmation in the proposal. Ask for separate descriptions of tableware, service duties, washing, waste handling and room handover.

**How early should we confirm the final guest count?**

Confirm the final guest count by the deadline agreed with your caterer. Ask for that deadline during the enquiry and establish how later changes will be handled.

**What should we send when requesting a corporate Christmas catering quote?**

Send the date, location, expected guest count and service required. Add the event schedule, dietary requirements, venue facilities and any access restrictions so the proposal addresses the actual event.

- [Catering for co-working spaces in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/catering-for-co-working-spaces-in-dubai-complete-guide)
- [Connecting office facilities management to lunch catering](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/how-to-connect-office-facilities-management-to-lunch-catering)

## One last check before you enquire

Write down who receives the room after the party and what condition they expect it in. That question turns an ambiguous request for cleanup into a clear handover requirement.

To discuss your corporate Christmas event with myCHEF, send the **date, location, guest count and service required**. Include your preferred format and venue arrangements so the enquiry starts with a usable brief.
